slides.title: What is a Prompt?
content: AI is a powerful tool, but it needs clear instructions.
A prompt is your instruction, question, or command to an AI.
Think of it as talking to a super-smart, but very literal, assistant.
Good prompts help AI give you exactly what you want.
narration: Imagine you have a very smart assistant.
They can do anything, but need clear instructions.
This is what a 'prompt' is for AI. It is your instruction.
A good prompt helps AI give you exactly what you want.
Mastering prompts helps you unlock AI's full potential.
slides.image_prompt: A person typing into a glowing AI interface, with abstract thought bubbles showing AI generating various outputs from the text input, emphasizing the concept of 'instruction to AI'.

slides.title: Be Clear, Be Specific
content: Rule 1: Don't make the AI guess! State exactly what you want.
Avoid vague language for better outputs.
Use the 5 W's and H: Who, What, When, Where, Why, How.
Weak: 'Write something about cats.'
Better: 'Write a short positive paragraph about benefits of owning a cat for busy professionals, focusing on stress relief.' (Adds Who, What, Why, When).
narration: The first rule is: Be clear and specific.
Don't make the AI guess. State exactly what you want.
For example, 'Write something about cats' is too vague.
A better prompt specifies: 'Write a short, positive paragraph.'
'Focus on benefits of owning a cat for busy professionals.'
'Highlight stress relief after a long workday.'
This prompt adds details like Who, What, When, and Why.
It helps the AI give a much more targeted response.
Being specific guides the AI to produce accurate and useful outputs.
slides.image_prompt: Two distinct text bubbles: one with vague, generic text like 'write about cats', leading to a blurred or generic image; the other with a clear, detailed prompt leading to a sharp, specific image of a cat comforting a professional. Visually contrast vague vs. specific.

slides.title: Add Context and Role
content: Give AI necessary background information to understand your needs.
Tell AI who to be (e.g., 'Act as a friendly chef').
Specify the target audience (e.g., 'for teenagers').
Weak: 'Give me a recipe.'
Better: 'Act as a friendly home cook. Provide a simple, healthy recipe for a quick weeknight dinner, for a family of four. Tone: encouraging.'
narration: Next, add context and role-play.
Tell the AI its situation and who it should act as.
Instead of 'Give me a recipe,' try: 'Act as a friendly, busy home cook.'
'Provide a simple, healthy recipe for a quick weeknight dinner.'
'It should take under 30 minutes for a family of four, with an encouraging tone.'
This guides the AI to generate a very specific and useful recipe.
Adding context ensures the AI understands your specific needs.
Role-playing shapes the AI's persona and output style.
slides.image_prompt: An AI chatbot interface with two inputs. One input shows a simple query, the other shows a detailed query including 'Act as a [role]' and 'Target audience: [group]'. Visuals for a chef, teacher, and marketer personas float around the detailed prompt.

slides.title: Set Boundaries and Give Examples
content: Define the structure: bullet points, essay, table.
Specify length: 'under 100 words', 'three paragraphs'.
Dictate desired style or tone: formal, casual, humorous.
For a very specific style, provide an example.
Excellent: 'Write three bullet points about cat benefits. Here's a style I like: 'Purr-Fect Companionship: Cats offer silent support...'.' (Expert)
narration: Finally, set boundaries and provide examples.
Tell the AI the format, length, and style you want.
For example, 'Write three bullet points about cat benefits for busy professionals.'
Then, provide an example of the desired style.
Like: 'Purr-Fect Companionship: Cats offer silent support, reducing loneliness.'
This way, the AI will perfectly mimic the desired tone and conciseness.
Setting boundaries helps control the AI's output structure.
Examples guide the AI to match your preferred style precisely.
slides.image_prompt: A graphic showing different output formats (bullet points, paragraph, table) with labels for 'length' and 'style'. An example text bubble illustrates a specific writing style next to it, showing how AI can replicate it.

slides.title: Key Takeaways
content: Be Clear & Specific: Avoid ambiguity.
Add Context: Give AI background information.
Role-Play: Tell AI who to be and its audience.
Set Constraints: Define format, length, and style.
Iterate & Refine: Use follow-up prompts.
narration: To summarize, remember our Prompting Checklist:
Be Clear and Specific. Avoid ambiguity.
Add Context. Give the AI background information.
Use Role-Play. Tell the AI who to be and its audience.
Set Constraints. Define format, length, and style.
And finally, Iterate and Refine your prompts in a conversation with the AI.
slides.image_prompt: A stylized checklist graphic, with each key takeaway point visually represented by a small icon (e.g., magnifying glass for clarity, a speech bubble for role-play, a ruler for constraints, arrows for iteration).

slides.title: Assignment
content: Task: Plan a surprise sci-fi themed birthday party for a friend who loves board games.
1. Write a basic prompt for ideas.
2. Refine it: Add AI role (e.g., 'party planner'), and details about your friend.
3. Further refine: Specify output format (bullet points for themes, activities, food) and tone (fun, creative).
Use an AI tool and practice!
narration: Here is a small assignment for you.
Imagine planning a surprise party. Your friend loves sci-fi and board games.
You want the AI to brainstorm ideas.
First, write a basic prompt.
Next, refine it by adding context.
Tell the AI to act as a party planner.
Finally, refine it further. Specify output format, like bullet points.
Include themes, activities, and food.
Also, set a fun and creative tone.
Try it out with an AI tool and practice!
